messages:
Ash: Quick update — I sketched a paginated-KV allocator that groups block-table entries by "live-span" instead of simple LRU buckets. Ran a quick smoke on seq=2048 LRU workload, memory compaction improved ~18% and average alloc latency dropped ~22%.

Kevin: Can you paste the allocation policy? curious how you define live-span buckets.

Ash: Sure — super simple for the prototype:
```
policy:
  live_span_buckets: 8
  hot_threshold_ms: 50
  coalesce_on_free: true
  eviction_prio: [shortest_live_span, oldest]
```
This biases toward returning contiguous slabs for long-lived KV segments so we get fewer fragmented pages.

Li: Nice. Did you try with our paged-attn batcher? fragmentation interacts badly with large batch tails.

Ash: Yup. With the batcher at target_batch=16 we saw steady throughput but the tail p95 dropped from 42ms -> 30ms on our infra-3 (A100-like) nodes. For small sequence workloads (<=128) flash-variants still win for raw kernel throughput, but our allocator helps multi-tenant steady-state.

Dana: Any regressions observed? I recall a prior attempt increased GC churn on infrequent frees.

Ash: Good call — in one run we saw a spike when bursty frees created many small holes. Fix was to attempt on-free coalescing and a deferred compaction pass that runs under low load. That removed the GC spike.

perf-bot: Benchmark summary (quick):
- baseline (LRU bucket): p50=11.9ms, p95=42.3ms, mem=12.1GB
- live-span allocator (proto): p50=9.3ms, p95=30.1ms, mem=9.9GB
- fused-attn opt (same infra): throughput +12% on seq=512, but +0% on seq=32 (kernel overheads)

Sam: Where should we land this? RFC + microbench harness? Also flag to kernel-selector to prefer fused kernels when occupancy > 60%?

Kevin: I'll open an RFC draft. We need two things: (1) metricized compaction plan + safety knobs (max compaction ms per second), (2) add a perf job that runs mixed seq-length traffic and reports mem-frag and tail-latency.

Ash: Sounds good. I'll push prototype branch with allocator toggle and perf harness logs. @Kevin please add the safety knobs in the RFC. :thumbsup:

Dana: Also add a short matrix that shows which FlashAttention variant we prefer by sequence-length + KV-pager state — that helped us elsewhere.

Ash: Will do. End plan: RFC + perf job + kernel-selector tweak. Low-risk rollout behind feature flag.
